history.note: Initial under-representation baseline — many common patterns (ko, ngs, nce) are near-zero in generated output. Thresholds start at 0; ratchet up as generator improves.
Post lexicon outlier retune (5x200k, morphology on): worst over-rep `ds` (3.8618x) and `pre` (2.9192x), thresholds set to +10%.
Post lexicon outlier retune under-rep ratchet: worst common under-rep `mc` (0.0317x) and `sio` (0.0069x), thresholds set to -10%.
Post length-semantics + scoring refactor retune: worst common under-rep bigram moved to `mc` (0.0241x). Floor set to -10% margin; trigram floor unchanged.

Hard c respell (#460/#469): root-final /k/ c is no longer doubled to `cc` before an e/i/y suffix (broccest, cacliccer), which read /ks/. Those were 25 of 26 `cc` in a 20k sample, so `cc` fell from 0.13-0.16x to 0.0133/0.0168/0.0099/0.0183/0.0099x (seeds 42/123/456/789/1337) and is now the worst common bigram. Floor set to -10% of 0.0099. Next worst: `gh`/`mc` 0.064-0.077x (main 0.061-0.077x).

#491: cc is report-only. The old PR's floor (0.0031x) requires about six hits per 200,000 words, versus a ten-seed mean of 9.6. All traced baseline and candidate hits come from -able, now sampled at the measured rate. A hard floor at this scale confuses sampling noise with a spelling defect. Other bigram floors stand.

#491: the earlier surface floors primarily measured over-weighted -ian/-ial and other suffix joins. The seed-2028 trace on main attributes 480 of 486 ia hits and all 191 ian hits to joins or affixes. Lower measured affix rates reduce those surface counts. A separate traced test checks that ia remains reachable in the root.

_comment: Quality ratchet: after each tuning fix, re-run 5× analysis (seeds 42/123/456/789/1337), update thresholds to new max + 10% margin (over-rep) or new min - 10% margin (under-rep), commit as part of fix PR.
